investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck unscheduled for 121–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes regardless of total cluster size. If those 2 nodes lost their kata.peerpods.io/vm label or taint, the pool would appear fully exhausted even with idle hardware.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if cleanup failed in a previous run, VM slots may be held by stale agents, reducing available capacity. No cleanup failure evidence is present in this packet, so this remains speculative.

Quaternary — cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to provision new kata-capable nodes in time: the scheduler message 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' and zero preemption victims suggest no lower-priority pods exist to evict, and no new node was added within the eval window.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T05:15–05:20Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production remote-agent swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent for a "remote" agent type (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905), the resulting pod was left Unschedulable for 144 seconds before the check timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent identity or state was produced, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the observability eval.

If those 2 nodes are saturated, no preemption is possible and the pod is permanently Unschedulable until capacity is freed.

With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), the pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds until the eval timed out. This is a cluster-infrastructure-level failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production outage is present in the supplied packet; this is an eval-environment scheduling failure.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck unscheduled for 121–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 146s, latencyMs=148706

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which must schedule a pod before any evidence can be written
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes regardless of total cluster size. If those 2 nodes lost their kata.peerpods.io/vm label or taint, the pool would appear fully exhausted even with idle hardware.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent VMs from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if cleanup failed in a previous run, VM slots may be held by stale agents, reducing available capacity. No cleanup failure evidence is present in this packet, so this remains speculative.

Quaternary — cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to provision new kata-capable nodes in time: the scheduler message 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' and zero preemption victims suggest no lower-priority pods exist to evict, and no new node was added within the eval window.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-create eval that produces vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would indicate the exhaustion was transient and has self-resolved.

Cluster inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unused on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes would disprove resource exhaustion and point instead to a pod spec or API error preventing scheduling.

Add a time-to-schedule latency eval that alerts at warning threshold when pod scheduling takes longer than a configurable baseline (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure before it causes full Unschedulable failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T05:15–05:20Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were collected, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production remote-agent swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent for a "remote" agent type (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905), the resulting pod was left Unschedulable for 144 seconds before the check timed out. Because the pod never started, no agent identity or state was produced, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both nodes that match the pod's affinity, leaving zero schedulable capacity. This directly explains all three sibling failures.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, meaning the effective scheduling pool is only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are saturated, no preemption is possible and the pod is permanently Unschedulable until capacity is freed.

Tertiary — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots: if other production or eval-triggered remote agents were running at the time of the eval, they may have consumed all available kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, leaving none for the eval pods.

Lower confidence — node affinity configuration drift: if the node selector or affinity rules on the remote-agent pod spec were recently tightened, the effective pool of eligible nodes may have shrunk, making exhaustion more likely. No suspect changes in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges support this hypothesis at this time.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed between 05:15 and 05:20 UTC on 2026-07-15 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence payload—leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler in the production-api environment was unable to place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable slots remaining), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), the pod remained Unschedulable for 146 seconds until the eval timed out. This is a cluster-infrastructure-level failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production outage is present in the supplied packet; this is an eval-environment scheduling failure.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduling error class, pod stuck unscheduled for 121s, endedAt 2026-07-15T05:15:08.467Z — the earliest sibling failure, indicating the resource exhaustion predates the runtime check.

sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduling error class, pod stuck unscheduled for 144s, endedAt 2026-07-15T05:17:36.526Z — confirms the resource pool was still exhausted across consecutive eval runs.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148706, status=fail — the eval ran to near-timeout before failing, consistent with a pod stuck in Pending rather than an immediate API error.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent — consistent with the agent never being created because the pod never scheduled.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was collected at all, confirming the probe never reached the agent runtime.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId; if the pod never schedules, no downstream evidence can be produced.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, confirming the runtime check is non-gating but still reflects the same underlying infrastructure failure.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, meaning the 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability. The combination of affinity restriction and VM exhaustion leaves no valid placement target.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or concurrent workload consumed the last kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and did not release them before this eval window, causing cascading failures across all three sibling checks in sequence (create at 05:15, state at 05:17, runtime at 05:20).

Lower confidence — the eval probe itself may not have a cleanup path that reliably releases kata VM resources on failure, potentially contributing to slot exhaustion across repeated runs. The runner uses withCleanup (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1916) but whether that cleanup successfully deallocates kata VM slots on scheduling failure is not confirmed by the supplied evidence.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Observe whether the pod scheduling error recurs or whether the pod schedules successfully.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling dependency
reproductionSteps.details: If all three fail with the same Unschedulable message, the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe node) to check the allocatable and allocated counts for the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on each node that matches the pod's affinity. Confirm whether slots are at zero.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for stuck or leaked remote agent pods in the eval namespace
reproductionSteps.details: List pods in the namespace used by the eval runner and look for any pods in Pending, Running, or Terminating state that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up.

affectedAreas.label: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool (production cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reported 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes eligible for remote agent pods. This is the binding constraint preventing pod scheduling (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod node affinity / node selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata-capable nodes and leaving no fallback placement target (evidence: failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with the same scheduling error class in the same eval window, indicating the entire remote agent provisioning path is blocked by the infrastructure constraint (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state, failed-check.message, source-context features.json:181-189).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner remote agent creation path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers pod scheduling. If the pod cannot schedule, no evidence is produced and the contract fails entirely (evidence: source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

recommendedNextActions: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible production cluster nodes immediately to determine whether the pool is still exhausted or has recovered.
Identify and terminate any stuck or leaked remote agent pods in the eval namespace that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads.

Review the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm it correctly releases kata VM resources when a pod fails to schedule (Unschedulable state), and add explicit cleanup for the Pending/Unschedulable case if it is missing.

Assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool size on the 2 eligible nodes is sufficient for concurrent eval runs plus any production workloads sharing the same resource, and consider increasing pool capacity or adding eligible nodes if the ceiling is routinely hit.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in infra/evals/status/features.json (lines 183-184) and the feature has degradedAfterFailures=1, confirm the feature's health status was correctly set to degraded or outage in the observability dashboard for this run window.

Re-run the full remote-agents eval suite after any cluster remediation to confirm all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return passing status and produce the expected evidence fields.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is still active or was transient. A pass confirms capacity was restored; a repeat of the same Unschedulable message confirms sustained exhaustion (evidence: verifierContext.recommendedVerifierProbes).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes whether the VM slot pool is exhausted and on which nodes, providing the ground-truth capacity state at investigation time.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run cluster node inspection tooling against the production cluster to retrieve the allocatable and requested counts for the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on each node.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources in the eval namespace
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If prior eval runs left pods in a non-terminal state, they would be holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling. Confirming or ruling out leaked pods is essential to understanding whether this is a capacity ceiling or a leak.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query the cluster for pods requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm in the namespace used by the eval runner to identify any leaked or stuck pods consuming slots.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared scheduling dependency causes all three checks to fail together, which would validate the single-root-cause hypothesis and help scope the impact to the kata VM pool.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated eval source paths for cleanup behavior on scheduling failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If cleanup does not fire on Unschedulable pods, repeated eval runs could accumulate leaked slot reservations, explaining why all three sibling checks failed in sequence within the same window.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Review infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs around the withCleanup call (line 1916) to determine whether the cleanup path is invoked and whether it releases kata.peerpods.io/vm resources when the pod never reaches Running state.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots greater than zero at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be identified.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on an immediate re-run without any cluster changes, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior workload released slots) rather than a sustained capacity deficit.
If the pod scheduling error message changes on re-run (e.g., a different error class such as an API authentication failure or quota error), the kata VM exhaustion would not be the root cause.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also failed in the same eval window with a similar scheduling error, it would suggest a broader cluster scheduling problem rather than one specific to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool.
If the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs is confirmed to always release kata VM resources even on scheduling failure, the leaked-slot hypothesis would be disproved as a contributing factor.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on each eligible node before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing pool exhaustion as a distinct, early-failing check rather than a timeout buried in the agent creation path.
Add a pre-flight eval that verifies no leaked or stuck remote agent pods are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots in the eval namespace, running before the remote-agent-create check.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are released after each remote agent eval cycle, catching resource leaks before they accumulate across runs.

Consider a synthetic eval that monitors the ratio of allocated to allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and fires a warning before the pool reaches zero, providing earlier signal than a full scheduling failure.
